_about: How the exposure lens groups what a footprint exposes to the internet. It reads the services the services lens finds and the URLs of the footprint, and puts each in the first class whose ports (the port numbers the IANA registry assigns the protocol), service_types, title_patterns (regular expressions over the page title a probe stored for the service as its title_property property), url_fields (URL content fields that are not empty, such as a password written into the URL), url_patterns (regular expressions over the URL) or txt_patterns (regular expressions over the DNS TXT records stored for a controlled name, read only when a class has them) match. A URL is always shown with any password in it masked. Each class says why reaching it from the internet matters. Services on unusual ports and certificates that expired or were self-issued are reported from the services lens as well. Add classes and values here, not in Go code.

classes.name: remote_access
classes.title: Remote access and shells
classes.rationale: remote logins are the first thing password guessing and exploits target; Telnet sends passwords in the clear

classes.name: databases
classes.title: Databases and data stores
classes.rationale: data stores reachable from the internet are a common source of data exposure

classes.name: file_sharing
classes.title: File sharing and transfer
classes.rationale: file shares and plaintext file transfer leak data and credentials

classes.name: management
classes.title: Infrastructure management interfaces
classes.rationale: device, container and cluster management interfaces give control of the systems behind them

classes.name: url_credentials
classes.title: URLs with an embedded password
classes.rationale: a password written into a URL is kept in browser history, server and proxy logs and wherever the link is shared, so treat it as disclosed and change it

classes.name: internal_details_in_dns
classes.title: TXT records that disclose internal details
classes.rationale: Kubernetes ExternalDNS ownership records name the cluster owner and the namespaces and resources behind public names

classes.name: login_pages
classes.title: Login and administration pages
title_patterns: (?i)\b(sign[ -]?in|log[ -]?in|log[ -]?on|single sign[ -]?on|sso|authentication|admin|administration|administrator|control panel|management console|webmail|outlook web app|remote desktop|vpn)\b
classes.rationale: login and administration pages, found by their path or page title, are targeted by credential stuffing and are often left unprotected by mistake
